SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 (Copyright 2023 Smith & Wesson Inc. All rights reserved.)
cleanIntro: The M&P22 Magnum's barrel sits inside a separate barrel shroud (the TEMPO barrel system), and the two come out of the slide together and then separate. The gap between them is where this pistol fouls, so the barrel and shroud are the heart of every clean. Deep Clean is the magazine, which the manual documents on its own.

steps.title: 22 WMR with jacketed bullets only
steps.action: Check what you have been shooting and what is going back in the box. This pistol takes the cartridge marked on the barrel, and the manual is emphatic that the bullets must be jacketed: FMJ, TMJ, JHP, JSP, or a jacketed bullet with a polymer tip. Copper-plated or polymer-coated bullets cause reliability problems, and birdshot loads will not reliably function in it.
steps.prose: This is a cleaning step as much as an ammunition one. If non-jacketed ammunition has been through the pistol, the clearance between the barrel and the barrel shroud leads up and fouls quickly, and the pistol will not run again until that gap has been cleaned thoroughly. Knowing what was fired tells you how hard the barrel and shroud clean below has to be.
steps.quote: Smith & Wesson® wants to emphasize that jacketed bullets MUST be used in the M&P® 22 MAGNUM pistol. Ammunition with copper-plated, or polymer-coated bullets will cause reliability issues.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Ammunition, notes regarding 22 WMR ammunition, p.10
steps.warn: NEVER USE CARTRIDGES OTHER THAN THOSE DESIGNATED BY THE MARKING ON THE FIREARM.

steps.title: Safety up, magazine out, slide drawn back to cock the hammer
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and outside the guard. Push the manual thumb safety lever fully up into SAFE, press the magazine release and remove the magazine, then grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear and briskly draw it fully rearward to extract anything in the chamber. Drawing the slide back also cocks the hammer, which this pistol needs before the slide can come off.
steps.prose: The cocked hammer is not a detail you can skip: the manual makes it the condition for removing the slide at all, and the same rule comes back when you reassemble. A slow pull on a rimfire can drag a case partway out and drop it back into the action, so pull the slide briskly and all the way.
steps.quote: The hammer of the M&P® 22 MAGNUM must be in the “cocked” position prior to attempting to remove the slide.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, note regarding disassembly procedure, p.25

steps.title: Lock the slide open, then look in the chamber and the magazine well
steps.action: Hold the slide fully rearward and press up on the slide stop lever to lock it open. Look into the chamber and make certain it is empty, then look down through the magazine well and make certain no ammunition is there. Unload the magazine separately by pressing each cartridge forward and out.
steps.prose: Two looks, because they can disagree. This pistol has no magazine disconnect: it can fire with the magazine out, so an empty magazine well proves nothing about the chamber. Keep your finger off the trigger until both checks are done.
steps.quote: Lock the slide open by holding it fully rearward and pressing up on the slide stop lever (FIGURE 44).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.26
steps.warn: THE M&P® 22 MAGNUM PISTOL CAN BE FIRED WHEN THE MAGAZINE IS REMOVED FROM THE PISTOL.

steps.title: Look at the breech face for a protruding firing pin
steps.action: With the slide open, look at the breech face and make sure the firing pin is not sticking out of it. If it is protruding, stop: do not load or fire the pistol, and take it to a gunsmith qualified to work on Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.prose: The manual builds this check into its inspection routine and asks for it every time the pistol is cleaned or changes hands. A stuck-forward firing pin is a fault that cleaning will not fix, and it is far better found on the bench than on the range.
steps.quote: If the firing pin is protruding (FIGURE 15c), do not attempt to load or fire the firearm.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Inspecting Your Pistol, p.14

steps.title: Find the takedown pin and close the slide
steps.action: Find the slide stop lever/takedown pin on the right side of the pistol, as viewed from the rear. Then grasp the serrated sides of the slide, draw it rearward until the slide stop disengages, and let the slide move forward to its closed position.
steps.prose: On this pistol the slide stop lever and the takedown pin are one part, and you push it out from the right side, not the left. The slide has to be closed for the next step, where you line the takedown notch up with the raised part of the pin.
steps.quote: until the slide stop disengages, then allow the slide to move forward to it’s closed position.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.26

steps.title: Slide back about 1/4 inch, then drift the pin out from the right
steps.action: Grasp the slide and push it back about a quarter of an inch, so that the takedown notch in the slide lines up with the raised part of the slide stop lever/takedown pin. Hold the slide there and use a small punch or drift to push the pin out of the frame from the right side.
steps.prose: If the pin will not move, the notch is not lined up. Adjust the slide position rather than hitting the punch harder. The slide stays under recoil spring tension the whole time, so keep a firm hold on it while the pin comes out.
steps.quote: While holding the slide with the takedown notch aligned, use a small punch or drift to push the Slide stop lever/Takedown pin out of position from the right side (FIGURES 52 and 53).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.27

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, controlling the recoil spring
steps.action: With the pin out, loosen your grip on the slide and push or pull it forward off the frame. Keep control of the recoil spring as the slide comes free.
steps.prose: The recoil spring assembly rides against the barrel shroud lug inside the slide, and it can spring loose as the slide leaves the rails. Keep the slide upside down in your hand so nothing drops out.
steps.quote: Retain control of the recoil spring when the slide is removed from the frame.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out of the slide
steps.action: Take the recoil spring assembly out of the slide: compress the spring slightly and lift it up and out.
steps.prose: Look at how its base sits against the barrel shroud lug before you lift it. On reassembly the base goes back against that lug and the guide rod has to sit centred on it.
steps.quote: by compressing the spring slightly and lifting it up and out (FIGURE 56).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Barrel and barrel shroud out of the slide as one unit
steps.action: Take the barrel and the barrel shroud out of the slide together: grasp both by the barrel shroud lug and lift up and back.
steps.prose: They come out as one piece, held by the lug, and you separate them only once they are out of the slide. Lifting by the barrel alone leaves the shroud behind and gives you nothing to grip.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel and barrel shroud as a unit from the slide by grasping the two parts by the barrel shroud lug and lifting up and back (FIGURE 57).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Separate the barrel from the barrel shroud
steps.action: Draw the barrel out of the barrel shroud so the two lie as separate parts, ready for cleaning.
steps.prose: This is the separation the cleaning section depends on. The fouling that stops this pistol builds up between the outside of the barrel and the inside of the shroud, and you can only reach it with the two apart. Smith & Wesson recommends taking them out and cleaning them at least every 500 rounds.
steps.quote: (FIGURE 59) shows the M&P® 22 MAGNUM barrel and barrel shroud being separated.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Slide assembly, frame assembly, barrel, barrel shroud, recoil spring assembly, slide stop lever/takedown pin, and magazine. The manual's field strip ends here, and you should not take the pistol apart any further. Never dry-fire this pistol at any point. Deep Clean covers the magazine, which the manual documents on its own.
steps.prose: The dry-fire rule on a rimfire is not a formality: with no case rim to stop it, the firing pin strikes the chamber edge. Anything beyond this field strip is gunsmith work under the manual's own warning.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, WARNING, p.29
steps.warn: DO NOT DRY-FIRE THE M&P® 22 MAGNUM PISTOL. DOING SO CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE PISTOL.

deepSteps.title: Empty magazine, depress the floor plate catch through the hole
deepSteps.action: With the magazine empty and wearing safety glasses, push a small-diameter tool such as a punch or drift through the hole in the bottom of the floor plate to depress the floor plate catch. Let the floor plate move just enough to keep the catch held down.
deepSteps.prose: The catch is the tab that locks the floor plate, and the spring underneath it pushes it up. Keep the base of the magazine pointed away from your face from this point.
deepSteps.quote: Allow the floor plate to move just enough to keep the catch depressed (FIGURE 83).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Magazine Disassembly, p.34
deepSteps.warn: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE IN THE ASSEMBLED MAGAZINE.

deepSteps.title: Slide the floor plate forward and off under control
deepSteps.action: Holding the floor plate catch down in the tube against the spring, slide the floor plate forward and off the magazine tube.
deepSteps.prose: The spring and catch are loose once the plate clears the tube. Keep a thumb over the opening as the plate comes off.
deepSteps.quote: While holding floor plate catch in the tube against spring pressure, slide floor plate forward and off the magazine tube (FIGURE 84).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Magazine Disassembly, p.34

deepSteps.title: Catch, spring and follower out the bottom of the tube
deepSteps.action: Take the floor plate catch, the spring and the follower out through the bottom of the tube. Note which way the spring sits before it comes out.
deepSteps.prose: The spring only works one way round, narrow end up with its slope against the follower, so note its orientation now and you won't have to guess on reassembly. Clean the inside of the tube and the follower while it is apart.
deepSteps.quote: Remove floor plate catch, the spring, and follower out through bottom of tube.
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
For The M&P® 22 MAGNUM Pistol — REV: M&P22_MAGNUM_04042023 — Magazine Disassembly, p.34

cleaning.name: BARREL AND BARREL SHROUD
tasks: Soak the barrel and barrel shroud in CLP for several hours in a container that holds both
Use brushes, picks and CLP to clean carbon and residue off the outside of the barrel and the inside of the shroud
Clean fouling from every surface and from the barrel gas port
Use non-marring tools on all surfaces so you don't damage the finish
Wipe everything with a clean rag to take off debris and excess CLP
Clean the bore from breech toward muzzle with a bore brush, jag and patches of the right size

cleaning.name: SLIDE AND FRAME
tasks: Clean the breech face and the inside of the slide
Clean the frame rails and around the takedown pin hole
Clean the outside of the pistol with a non-abrasive cloth and remove all solution, oil and fingerprints

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the magazine tube and feed lips
If the magazine has been apart, clean inside the tube and the follower before reassembly
Check that the floor plate is locked in place before the magazine goes back into service

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Put a single drop of high-quality firearm lubricant on each of the eight lubrication points the manual shows, with the pistol field stripped
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts inside and out with a high-quality gun oil
Do not over-lubricate: excess oil collects unburned powder and carbon residue and can interfere with function
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this pistol

reassembly: Put the barrel back into the barrel shroud. It fits against the shroud only one way.
Put the barrel assembly back into the slide: start the muzzle end into the hole at the front of the slide, then tip the rear of the barrel assembly down into position.
Install the recoil spring assembly with its base against the barrel shroud lug, and seat the recoil spring/guide rod so it is centred on the lug.
Make sure the hammer is cocked. If it sticks up above the frame in the fired position, push it down and back until it is cocked.
Holding the recoil spring in place, push the slide onto the front frame rails, then back onto the rear frame rails.
Pull the slide rearward until the takedown notch lines up with the hole in the frame, hold it about 1/4 inch back, and insert the slide stop lever/takedown pin until it clicks into place.
Let go and allow the slide to move forward to its closed position.

Magazine: install the follower, spring and floor plate catch in the tube, with the spring's narrow end at the top and its slope against the follower. Push the catch and spring down, slide the floor plate fully on, and apply light forward pressure to confirm it is locked.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed in a safe direction, grasp the rear slide serrations and draw the slide back to confirm it is installed correctly and moves freely. Check that the slide stop lever/takedown pin is fully clicked in. Insert an empty magazine, apply some removal pressure to its butt plate to confirm it is locked in place, then press the release and remove it. Never dry-fire this pistol to test the trigger.
